data.why: the repo ships no example slide images, so stock photos stand in: the multiwell plate's periodic grid structure exercises the full border-detection -> contour -> CNN-classification -> annotated-preview pipeline to a numeric count, while the plain coin photo has no slide border for getBorders() to find and so demonstrates the pipeline's count='error' path; the three seed files replace the repo's native showDirectoryPicker-based folder picker (which opens an OS dialog no browser automation can fill) with a standard multi-file <input type=file multiple> wired to the same per-image processing loop, and fill in the About tab's previously empty 'Using Countess' section

goals: Load a folder of counting-slide microscope images and get a per-image egg count without manual annotation
Visually verify which objects the CNN classified as eggs via the annotated preview image for each slide
Confirm that an image the pipeline cannot read (no detectable slide border) is reported as count='error' rather than silently skipped or miscounted
Export all per-image counts to a CSV for downstream statistical analysis
Process a batch of images unattended, with a visible progress indicator and a completion message once the whole folder has been counted

review.summary: The goal and main phases match what the README and paper say Countess is for: batch CNN counting of nematode eggs on counting-slide images, visual checking, error flagging, and CSV export. But the tree misreads the annotation overlay, states a CSV 'replace' behavior the code contradicts, and cites several screens that don't show the CSV or toast claims, so it needs those fixes before filing.
